name: Claude
tagline: AI assistant from Anthropic for chat, writing, coding and file work, with plans for individuals, teams, companies and universities

evidence.quote: Deleted from our back-end storage systems within 30 days
For Anthropic API users, we automatically delete inputs and outputs on our backend within 30 days of receipt or generation

retention_stated.note: For Claude for Work/Enterprise, chats are kept in the product until the user deletes them, then removed from back-end storage within 30 days. Enterprise admins can set custom retention periods. Exceptions: chats flagged for Usage Policy violations (inputs and outputs up to 2 years, classification scores up to 7 years) and feedback submissions (5 years).

deletion_on_exit.note: DPA section H.1: return a copy on request, then delete all copies of Customer Data, except where law requires, for a dispute, or to combat harmful use.

data_export.note: Team and Enterprise Primary Owners can export organization data via an emailed link; admins can also let users export their own chats (without uploaded file contents). The export file format is not stated. On Claude for Education, Primary Owner data exports are off by default and must be requested from Anthropic support.

evidence.quote: to train and improve Anthropic AI models
ElevenLabs Product: Claude for Work

ai_providers.note: Anthropic develops and runs the Claude models. ElevenLabs is listed as a text-to-speech subprocessor for Claude for Work (voice mode). Web search queries go to Brave Search, TurboPuffer and Parallel Web Systems (search services, not language models). Cloud providers host infrastructure (see cloud_providers).

evidence.quote: By default, we will not use your inputs or outputs from our commercial products
or otherwise choose to allow us to use your data, then we may use your chats and coding sessions to train our models
Anthropic may not train models on Customer Content from Services

trains_on_content.footnote: Institutional answer (Claude for Education, Team, Enterprise, API): no training by default; training only on conversations a user submits as feedback (thumbs up/down, bug reports) or if the organisation joins the Development Partner Program. Feedback is de-linked from user IDs and kept up to 5 years; admins can turn the feedback button off, and on Claude for Education it is off by default. Consumer plans (Free, Pro, Max, Ultra): training is on unless the user opts out, plus flagged and reported chats are used even after opt-out (pricing page: 'Model training: Opt-out').
trains_on_content.note: The Commercial Terms forbid training on Customer Content; the privacy center explains the exceptions where the customer explicitly reports or allows use, so the value is opt-in rather than a flat no.

evidence.quote: the only products to which zero data retention applies are eligible Anthropic APIs
subject to Anthropic’s approval, may have arrangements under which Anthropic does not store their inputs or outputs

ai_zero_retention.footnote: Zero data retention exists only as an approved arrangement for eligible Claude API use and Claude Code on Enterprise plans. It does not cover the Claude chat apps (Claude for Education, Team, Enterprise chat), where chats are stored until deleted. Even under ZDR, safety classifier results are kept, and Covered Models require limited retention.
ai_zero_retention.note: Anthropic is itself the model provider; there is no separate third-party model provider.

evidence.quote: Your organization determines which Claude services and features you can access in your Claude for Education account

ai_admin_off.footnote: Admins can limit individual features (for example web search, connectors, feedback, public projects). The AI assistant itself is the product, so it cannot be switched off other than by not giving users access.

incidents.note: Searched for a vendor notice or regulator decision. Press reports describe a South Korean PIPC investigation opened 2026-11-10 after Anthropic reported exposure of about 100 Korean business accounts; no regulator decision or Anthropic notice was found on primary sources, so nothing is recorded as fact. The Trust Center lists one security advisory (CVE-2026-22561, Windows installer), which is a vulnerability, not a breach.
